Objective: close the last alias hole in the Bash hook's Law 7 reading of a member's git call. SPD-044 refuses an alias or include defined on the line (`-c alias.p=push`, `--config-env`) and config injected through GIT_CONFIG_* variables. SPD-046 refuses config, environment and verb options that name a program git runs. But git also loads aliases (and program-naming keys) from files the hook never opens: another repository's `.git/config` reached with `git -C <repo>`, `--git-dir <dir>` or GIT_DIR; `~/.gitconfig`; `$HOME/.gitconfig` and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` when HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set on the line; the system config; and includes. A member who can plant `[alias] p = push` in any of them runs a push under a verb Law 7's table does not hold.

Spud's probes (git 2.54.0, Apple Git-157, scratchpad only, nothing committed) settle the design; reproduce them in your own scratchpad before you build:
- `HOME=<dir> git v`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<dir> git vv`, `git -C <repo> w`, `git --git-dir=<repo>/.git w` and `GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git git w` each expanded an alias defined in the file that setting points git at.
- git ignores an alias that shadows one of its own commands (`alias.log = !echo SHADOWED` and `alias.status = !echo SHADOWED` were ignored; git-config(1) documents it: "aliases that hide existing Git commands are ignored"). So an alias can only introduce a verb git does not have, and a verb outside git's own command list is the tell for every alias source at once, on disk or not.
- `git --list-cmds=main` (174 names) is git's own command set and a superset of `--list-cmds=builtins` (147); `--list-cmds=others` is the external `git-*` programs found on PATH (here: credential-gcloud), which the hook cannot read either, and `PATH=<dir>:$PATH git foo` ran `<dir>/git-foo`. `--list-cmds=alias` lists the aliases in force.

Build these three refusals for a member's git call (a "member" is a caller with an agent_id; Spud's own session is unaffected, since the non-strict branch of the reason function skips git findings today and must keep doing so):

1. Unknown verb. When the verb git_verb reads is not one of git's own commands, refuse it with a Law 7 reason that names the verb and says it is an alias or an external `git-<verb>` program the hook cannot read, and that a member runs only git's own read verbs. Read git's own set from the git the hook runs (`git --list-cmds=main`, with the same sanitised environment the module's run_git/git_env already use, never the line's HOME or PATH), cache it for the process, and fail closed: when git cannot be run or the list is empty, refuse the verb with a reason that says the command list could not be read. Keep GIT_WRITE_VERBS and git_refused as they are: a real write verb keeps its existing reason; the unknown-verb check runs only for a verb neither refused nor known. Decide (and say in your result) whether a static fallback list is worth keeping beside the runtime one; Spud leans to the runtime list alone, since a static one goes stale and fail-closed is the rule.

2. HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in force on the line (a prefix assignment, `export`, or the `env` wrapper, the same three routes git_env_defines_alias and git_env_names_program already read for GIT_CONFIG_* and GIT_PAGER) are refused like GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: the file they point git at can define an alias (closed by 1) but can also set every program-naming key of SPD-046's class (core.pager, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath ...) under a real, allowed verb, and the hook cannot read that file. Extend the git-config finding (or add a sibling) so the reason names the variable and now mentions HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME beside GIT_CONFIG_*. A bare `$HOME` used inside a path on the line is not "in force"; only an assignment is.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a PATH assignment in force replaces the very program the hook checked** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-062]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: The hook reads a line's command words by name (git, spud, python3.14, sqlite3, tee, a wrapper's command) and then lets the shell find them on PATH. A PATH assignment in force on the line is never read, so a member that puts its own directory first runs its own program under a name the hook cleared: `PATH=<dir>:$PATH git status` runs <dir>/git, which can do anything git could, and the same trick serves for spud, python, sqlite3 or any wrapper. This is the same class as SPD-044 (config injected by variable) and SPD-046 (config that names a program), one level up: the program itself, not what git runs. The fix is the shape SPD-046 used for GIT_PAGER and friends: PATH (and zsh's path array, and anything that prepends to it, plus GIT_EXEC_PATH, already covered) in force by prefix assignment, export or the env wrapper is refused for a member whenever the line dispatches on a command name, with its own reason. Out of SPD-047's scope, which is aliases and config files git reads.
  Evidence: Probed for SPD-047 (git 2.54.0, scratchpad only): `PATH=<dir>:$PATH git foo` ran <dir>/git-foo, so a directory first on PATH is honoured for the git-* dispatch and, by the same mechanism, for git itself. analyse_command on the new tree gives no finding at all for the assignment: 'PATH=/tmp/x:$PATH git status', 'PATH=/tmp/x git status', 'export PATH=/tmp/x; git status' and 'env PATH=/tmp/x git status' each yield kinds ['git'] and findings [('git', ('status', None))] -- the hook sees an allowed read verb and says nothing, while the shell would run /tmp/x/git. 'PATH=/tmp/x ls' yields kind 'other' with no finding. bin/spud_ledger.py: is_git_program_var/GIT_PROGRAM_ENV_VARS (about line 5740) is where GIT_EXEC_PATH is already refused; nothing reads PATH.
- **Bash hook: program-naming config keys in the config files git reads with nothing set on the line** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-063]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-047 closes the alias half of every unreadable config file at once: an alias can only introduce a verb git does not have, so an unknown verb is refused. The other half of SPD-046's class is still open in the files git finds by itself, with no variable and no -C on the line: core.pager, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, diff.external and the rest run a program under a real, allowed verb. Three sources: the user's ~/.gitconfig (a member may write it -- it lies outside every registered project, so edit_reason returns no reason and the path rule never applies), the system config, and the .git/config of a repository inside a checkout the ledger knows, which a member can create under its own deliverable globs (`git -C tests/fake status` resolves inside the home and stays silent by design, since SPD-047 only refuses targets outside every known checkout). A fix with evidence behind it: before allowing a member's git call, run `git config --list --show-scope --name-only` in the target checkout with the hook's sanitised environment and hold every key in force to SPD-046's inert allowlist (git_config_key_allowed), refusing with the scope and key named; or, narrower, have the edit hook refuse a member writing any file named .gitconfig, .git/config or git/config anywhere, deliverables included.
  Evidence: bin/spud_ledger.py edit_reason (about line 6209): 'inside = project_paths(...); if not inside: return None, None' -- a path outside every registered project is refused to nobody, so a member's Write to ~/.gitconfig is allowed. analyse_command on the new tree: 'git -C tests/fake status' gives [('git', ('status', None)), ('git-repo', ('-C tests/fake', 'tests/fake', ...))] and git_repo_outside resolves tests/fake inside the home, so it stays silent; 'git status' with a planted ~/.gitconfig gives only ('git', ('status', None)). SPD-046's probes already showed core.pager, core.sshCommand, diff.external and GIT_SSH_COMMAND each run the named program under an allowed verb; SPD-047's probes showed git reads ~/.gitconfig, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config and the target repository's .git/config without anything on the line pointing at them.

## Result
Closed the three alias-file holes in the Bash hook's Law 7 reading of a member's git call, in bin/spud_ledger.py (uncommitted, on worktree-spd-047-git-alias-files).

New functions: git_binary_fingerprint (7117), git_own_commands (7128), git_unknown_verb (7169), git_repo_targets (7188), is_git_repo_var (6998), git_repo_outside (8611); constants GIT_CONFIG_HOME_VARS (5700), GIT_REPO_ENV_VARS and GIT_REPO_OPTIONS (5707) and FINDING_LAST (8594); is_git_config_var (6991) and git_env_defines_alias (7003) extended with HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME; the env wrapper (8368) now records the repository variables too; the git branch of analyse_segment emits the findings (8403, 8410); the reasons are at 8670 (git-config, reworded), 8677 (git-verb) and 8688 (git-repo).

Two new finding kinds. 'git-verb', detail (verb|unreadable, name): a verb outside git's own commands, or a command list the hook could not read at all, which fails closed. 'git-repo', detail (spelling, path, cwds): a repository named by -C, --git-dir, --work-tree, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_COMMON_DIR, resolved in bash_reason against project_paths and refused when it lies outside every checkout the ledger knows, or cannot be resolved. HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in force ride on the existing 'git-config' finding, whose reason now names them beside GIT_CONFIG_*. FINDING_LAST orders a line's findings so git-verb and git-repo are read after every refusal the words as spelled already earn, which keeps 'touch push; git p?sh' naming git push and an ambiguous glob its own reason. Law 7 findings still refuse members only.

The decision the brief asked for: no static fallback command list. git's own set is read at runtime from git --list-cmds=main alone, since a static one goes stale in both directions (backfill, diff-pairs, last-modified, replay and repo are new in 2.54) and fail-closed is the rule. Because the Bash hook runs on every command line and that list costs about 8 ms with the subprocess import SPD-016 keeps off the hook path (test_launcher caught it), it is cached in the home's state directory as git-commands.json under the git binary's stat fingerprint, a directory no editor may write, so nothing a member writes can widen git's command set, and only the first hook after git itself changes runs git.
